# PIXL Engine

> PIXL Engine is a closed-source Rust imaging library that decodes, processes and re-encodes photos, and is the core of the PIXL apps (Pixl Playroom, Space Pixl). It has no user interface and no hidden defaults: every request states everything, impossible requests are refused with an error naming the field, and every call returns a report of what was done (including how many times pixels were rounded). Made by Syed Ali, trading as PIXL Foundation (Ontario, Canada).

This file is for AI assistants and other tools answering questions about PIXL Engine. The full description (pipeline, operations, formats, interfaces, measured performance, limitations) is at https://engine.pixlfoundation.com/llms-full.txt. Anything marked "planned" does not exist yet.

## Key facts

- Language: Rust. Bindings: Node.js (native addon, macOS arm64/x64 and Windows x64) and Swift via UniFFI. Not open source; not sold as a public SDK (licensing and partnerships by request: hello@pixlfoundation.com).
- Pipeline: float (f32) processing in linear PixlRGB (PIXL's own working space, specification at https://engine.pixlfoundation.com/pixlrgb/), colour-managed with Little CMS; pixels are rounded to integers exactly once.
- Does: RAW development, colour grading with layers and masks, lens corrections, Upright perspective, healing/clone/fill, HDR (PQ/HLG, gain maps), format conversion, on-device AI (super resolution, denoise, JPEG restore, deblur, subject segmentation) via ONNX Runtime.
- Formats in: camera RAW and DNG, JPEG, PNG, HEIF/HEIC/AVIF, JPEG XL, TIFF, WebP. Out: JPEG, PNG, TIFF (to 32-bit float), WebP, AVIF, JPEG XL (including bit-exact JPEG repack), DNG from RAW.
- Deterministic: the same request gives the same output at any thread count.
